name: secrets
description: Store and manage credentials safely; use secret references for integrations. Load before configuring an integration that needs credentials.

content.inline:
## Secrets
- Store an encrypted caller-scoped credential with `{name, value}` using the operation contributed by this skill. Existing secrets are protected: pass `overwrite: true` only when replacement is deliberate.
- Pass `s/<name>` wherever an operation accepts a secret reference, for example `apiKey: "s/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"`. Resolution happens at invocation time; the raw value is not copied into durable agent config.
- List names with the listing operation contributed by this skill; optional prefix, offset and limit keep results small. Workspace listing of `s` also works.
- Delete only on explicit user intent: identify the exact secret and explain that dependent integrations may stop working. Never delete as speculative cleanup. Deletion removes the stored copy, not the provider credential; provider-side revocation is separate. A missing secret returns `deleted:false`. Workspace deletion of a whole `s/<name>` record also works.

Rules:
- Choose callables from the current tool palette by their descriptions and schemas; do not construct their names from these instructions.
- Never put a raw key in agent config, workspace values, prompts, or other durable records. Job inputs redact declared secretFields, but arbitrary config/data does not.
- Secret names are per-user; an agent acting as a user resolves that user's store.
- MCP and HTTP authentication should also use secret references.
- Raw extraction is deliberately not included in this skill. `v/ops/secret/extract` is for direct owner-facing calls under `secret/extract` authority. It refuses MCP tools, agents, sessions, nested calls and recorded jobs. Do not offer extraction as an agent tool or ask users to paste its result into a conversation.
